A1.justification: Both PDFs describe 3MDBench and retain the same central framework. All 26 pages of v1 and 35 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable and support comparison. Reordered material can be matched; identifiable reporting inconsistencies do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original patient- and assessor-model comparisons, simulated medical consultations, diagnostic and clinical-competence results, and EfficientNetV2 experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and reports additional annotation-consistency analyses, diagnostic confusion matrices, and category-level results.

M1.justification: The documented consultation-scoring prompt changes the Assessor Agent's role from a group of medical experts in v1 Appendix A.4 to a patient in v2 Appendix F.4. The patient simulator, doctor strategies, and top-three EfficientNet prediction mechanism remain. Correcting the diagnosis-extraction prompt does not establish that an extractor was newly introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 34 diagnoses across five medical categories, four patient temperaments, and retained text/image consultation scenarios. Dataset names and diagnosis synonyms are matched across versions. The revised case count changes sample size, not demonstrated task or population coverage.

E2.justification: The six patient candidates, four assessor candidates, three doctor LVLMs, six GPT-4o-mini configurations, and EfficientNetV2 size comparisons remain. Corresponding comparison tables retain their participants. MediQ's addition to the related-benchmark table is descriptive positioning, not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 revises the benchmark size from 3,030 to 3,013 cases. V2 Appendix B reports excluding one of five annotators from the agreement calculation, changing its reference sample. Training/validation sizes, dialogue limits, and generation budgets remain. These reported revisions do not establish that all experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds annotator-consistency and exclusion analysis, disease-specific confusion matrices for GPT-4o-mini with rationale, and category-level competence and dialogue-length analyses. V1 Figure 6 already plots length by personality despite its diagnosis-category caption; v2 Figure 10 adds the actual category breakdown. Appendix H also replaces different-diagnosis dialogue illustrations with four eczema examples. These substantially extend supplementary and error analysis.

E5.justification: V2 Appendix B newly documents repeated annotation tasks and within-annotator consistency, alongside pairwise agreement and estimation after annotator exclusion. Wilcoxon testing at 0.01, Benjamini–Hochberg correction, and existing dialogue-length variability reporting remain. The changed rationale p-value is a changed statistical outcome, not evidence of a new significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Human agreement changes from 0.339 to 0.48; assessor kappas change from 0.31/0.33/0.28 to 0.36/0.43/0.32 for Qwen/LLaVA/GPT. Rationale prompting changes from nonsignificant, p=0.89, to significant, p<0.01, despite retained F1 scores of 56.9 versus 54.2. Disease- and temperament-specific F1 plots are numerically revised, and additional matrices and category results appear. Headline diagnostic and competence tables remain unchanged; the revisions do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Neither version contains substantive theoretical results or proofs. The task definitions and metric reasoning retain their meaning; simplifying complaint-set notation into prose does not introduce a mathematical change.

C1.justification: The central benchmark, temperament simulation, multimodal consultation, and CNN-cue contributions remain. V2's abstract and contribution list foreground internal reasoning as beneficial, reporting a 6.5% improvement over the non-dialogue baseline, whereas v1 foregrounds the dialogue-only increase from 50.4 to 54.2. The advertised approximately 20% cue benefit restates previously reported scores rather than introducing a new contribution.

C2.justification: V2 reverses the interpretation of rationale prompting: explanations alone now enhance diagnostic reasoning, whereas v1 says their benefit is not significant. It adds substantive limitations concerning synthetic symptom errors, assessor errors, pretraining leakage, disclosed candidate labels, and simplified temperaments. It also introduces a self-recognition-bias rationale for the patient-model choice and develops the interpretation of passive-patient interactions.

D1.justification: V2 supplies operational diagnosis-extraction instructions where v1 duplicated the consultation-scoring prompt. It adds annotation labor details and A100 inference times of 48, 4, and 210 hours for patient selection, assessor selection, and doctor evaluation. The advertised code location changes from GitHub to an anonymous 4open.science address. Most existing generation and CNN-training details remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds targeted references concerning visual diagnosis, clinical rater reliability, model self-recognition, and LLM judging. It supplies citations for previously listed benchmarks and adds MediQ to the comparison table. Some earlier references are removed, but the positioning around multimodal, temperament-aware medical dialogue remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and methodological narrative are extensively condensed and rewritten. Doctor-agent evaluation becomes Section 3.5, agent-selection results move into Section 4.1, and diagnostic-result discussions are consolidated. Appendices are substantially reordered, and separate Limitations and Ethics Statement sections are introduced.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reformats typography and page layout, moves the benchmark-comparison table into the main text, transposes the clinical-competence table, and redraws plots with revised axes, labels, legends, and ordering. The personality-competence figure moves to the appendix. New agreement, distribution, category-analysis, and confusion-matrix figures accompany rearranged and replaced case illustrations.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful error analyses, explicit limitations, extraction instructions, and resource disclosures. However, its stronger rationale claim changes p=0.89 to p<0.01 for unchanged headline scores without explaining the reversal. Appendix B also states annotator #1's mean kappa as 0.42 although Figure 8's four corresponding edges average 0.33. These unresolved reliability issues accompany the improved transparency, preventing a confident judgment of net improvement or deterioration.
